messages.subject: question about merging data frames
parts:

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: question about merging data frames
parts:
Maegen, 

Can you be more clear on what you want. 

You can merge data that is exactly the same treatment x replicate x date, but what do you want when the following happens?
"and if temp$date falls between fluxes$date1 and fluxes$date2"
"I think in some cases there will be >1 temp$date record, in which case I would want to average them."

I assume the value you are referring to is soil_temperature, is that right?

So far I have the following. 

#get the data in
temperature <- read.csv("~/Downloads/temperature.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
fluxes <- read.csv("~/Downloads/fluxes.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

#load muxing library
require(dplyr)

#take a look
glimpse(fluxes)
glimpse(temperature)

#Q: How many duplicates do you have?
temperature %>%
group_by(treatment, replicate, date) %>%
summarise(count = n() ) %>%
filter(count != 1)

#A: loads [82]

B

You can merge data that is exactly the same treatment x replicate x date, but what do you want when the following happens?
"and if temp$date falls between fluxes$date1 and fluxes$date2"

I want to create a new data frame that associates each flux record with a soil temperature (temperature$soil_temperature). The date which soil temperature was measured (i.e. temperature$date) must fall within the date range that flux was measured (fluxes$T0_Date to fluxes$T21_Date).

"I think in some cases there will be >1 temp$date record, in which case I would want to average them."
I assume the value you are referring to is soil_temperature, is that right?

Yes

This is what I have so far to read the data:
fluxes <- read.csv("fluxes.csv")
levels(fluxes$T0_Date)
levels(fluxes$T21_Date)

temp <- read.csv("temperature.csv")
levels(temp$date)

names(temp)[2]<-"Treatment"
names(temp)[3]<-"Replicate"
fluxes$T0_Date <- as.Date(fluxes$T0_Date, "%m/%d/%y") 
head(fluxes$T0_Date) #check

fluxes$T21_Date <- as.Date(fluxes$T21_Date, "%m/%d/%y")
head(fluxes$T21_Date) #check

temp$date <- as.Date(temp$date, "%m/%d/%Y")
dim(fluxes) #check

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: question about merging data frames
parts:
This should be close (the last line needs tweaking still but I have to run):


t <- read.csv("temperature.csv", stringsAsFactors=F)
f <- read.csv("fluxes.csv", stringsAsFactors=F)
names(f) <- tolower(names(f))

n <- merge(t, f, by=c("treatment","replicate"), all=T)

n$date <- as.Date(n$date, "%m/%d/%y")
n$t0_date <- as.Date(n$t0_date, "%m/%d/%y")
n$t21_date <- as.Date(n$t21_date, "%m/%d/%y")

n$t1 <- ifelse(n$date > n$t0_date & n$date < n$t21_date, 1, 0)

new <- n[which(n$t1 == 1),]

library(plyr)
test <- ddply(new, .(treatment, replicate, date), summarize, soil_temperature=mean(soil_temperature))
